---
title: "One day, data tools – the housing-audit case"
subtitle: "Four parts of ninety minutes, with a facilitator"
---
The [case study](../../cases/housing/index.qmd), which presents the original study, the Multi100 project, the five reanalyses and the SCORE replication on which every format of the case is built, is the place to start.

This is the one-day course on the housing-audit case with the tools of data science in the foreground: R, the IDE, data management, a Quarto report and version control. The case is the material for all of them. It is a field experiment, in which emails that differed only in the name that signed them were sent to public housing authorities in the United States, with a claim of the original authors (OAs) that five analysts reanalysed for Multi100. After a short opening on why reproducible tools matter, the morning takes the toolchain apart and gives you a first session in R on the emails of the case. In the afternoon you manage the data, from the file that the OAs published to the columns that an analysis needs, and the R work reaches its target: you reproduce one of the five reanalyses, whichever you choose, put the result into a report whose numbers come from the code, and check that the report survives a clean run. The day has no menu of specifications and sends nothing to a class chart; the [one-day course on methods](../housing-one-day-methods/index.qmd) does both.

The day is taught mainly in the [browser lab](../../cases/housing/lab.qmd), a page of the course site on which R runs inside your browser, with nothing to install. This is the format in which the downloadable workspace, opened in an IDE (Positron, RStudio, VS Code, etc.), gives you most, because the IDE and the report have parts of their own; if you have not installed it, you follow those parts on the shared screen and do the R in the lab. The day runs as four parts of ninety minutes, with breaks of thirty, sixty and thirty minutes between them, and it needs a facilitator. The same case is also taught as a [short session](../housing-short/index.qmd) and as a one-day course on [open science](../housing-one-day-open-science/index.qmd).

| | What happens | Length |
|---|---|---|
| [Before the day](before.qmd) | Read the case study and open the browser lab once; install R, an IDE and the workspace if you can, since this day uses them most. | about an hour, more with the installation |
| [Part 1 – Credibility and the toolchain](part-1.qmd) | The three Rs and the evidence on how often findings survive a check, then the toolchain layer by layer: languages, editors, file formats, rendering, packages, version control, archives and licences; then you get running. | 90 minutes |
| [Part 2 – R and the IDE](part-2.qmd) | The paper of the case, the IDE, and R from the beginning on the emails of the case; then you count and plot what came back. | 90 minutes |
| [Part 3 – Data management and the reproduction](part-3.qmd) | The public file and the course file, missing values, raw and derived files; then you reproduce one of the five reanalyses, and a second if there is time. | 90 minutes |
| [Part 4 – The report and its record](part-4.qmd) | A Quarto report from the inside and numbers that come from the code; you put your reproduction into the report, run it clean, and see how a project keeps its versions. | 90 minutes |
| [After the day](after.qmd) | Where to go next. | as you like |
